summary: Togo waives visas for ECOWAS citizens and, for stays of up to 30 days, for all other African nationals, while everyone else needs an eVisa applied for on voyage.gouv.tg at least six working days before travel — visas on arrival are suspended. Every traveller also completes the portal's online immigration form before arrival.

notes: Large amounts of cash should be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Togolese customs before carrying significant sums.

payments.text: Cash dominates. Cards are accepted only at larger hotels and supermarkets in Lomé, and ATMs are unreliable outside the capital. Mobile-money services are widely used locally; carry CFA francs for everyday spending.

safety.text: Most of Togo, including Lomé and the coast, is calm with mainly petty crime to watch for. Foreign governments advise against travel to the far-northern Savanes region bordering Burkina Faso because of a risk of terrorist incursions. Check current advisories before heading north.

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the main dry season — the best window for the beaches around Lomé, the Koutammakou landscape and hiking in the Plateaux region, though the harmattan can bring hazy skies.

idp.text: Togo is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Togo is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Togo yet.

tips.text: Avoid the Savanes region along the Burkina Faso border — foreign governments warn of a real terrorism risk there; the rest of the country is far calmer.
Apply for the eVisa only on the official voyage.gouv.tg portal — third-party visa websites charge heavy markups for the same document.
Keep your yellow fever certificate with your passport. It is checked on arrival and sometimes at land borders.
Withdraw or exchange CFA francs in Lomé before traveling upcountry. The same currency is used in Benin, Burkina Faso and other WAEMU neighbors, so leftover notes stay useful.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Togo?
faq.answer: Citizens of ECOWAS countries enter visa-free, and all other African nationals may stay up to 30 days without a visa. Everyone else needs the official eVisa from voyage.gouv.tg, applied for at least 6 working days before arrival: visas on arrival are suspended. All travellers must complete the online immigration form before arrival.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Togo?
faq.answer: Yes. Togo requires a yellow fever vaccination certificate from all arriving travelers, and the yellow card is checked on arrival — get vaccinated at least 10 days before your trip.

faq.question: Is Togo safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Lomé, the coast and the central Plateaux are generally safe, with petty theft the main concern. The exception is the far-northern Savanes region near Burkina Faso, where governments advise against travel due to terrorism risk. Check current advisories before planning a route north.

faq.question: Can I enter Togo overland from Ghana or Benin?
faq.answer: Yes. The coastal crossings at Aflao (Ghana) and Hillacondji (Benin) are busy and straightforward for ECOWAS citizens. Other nationalities who need a visa must arrive with an approved eVisa, since visas on arrival are suspended.
